newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS cargo unit clarifies fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: SAS cargo unit clarifies fuel surcharge.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS's cargo unit on Wednesday clarified that its increase in freight prices, announced a day ago, was actually a fuel surcharge.
"On cargo it is a fuel surcharge," Kim Moeller of SAS Cargo marketing told Reuters.

"It varies from airline to airline, but in our case it's between five and 10 U.S. cents and is specified on the airway bill as a charge called "due carrier" and will go to the airline to which the airway bill belongs," Moeller said.
He said on short-haul flights within Europe the surcharge would amount to five cents and on overseas flights, 10 cents.
SAS announced on Tuesday it was increasing passenger ticket prices by 2.0 percent and freight price by 5.0 percent due to higher fuel costs from November 15.
But on the passenger side the price hike was designated an increase, said Britta Larsson, manager for the Scandinavian flag carrier's European passenger ticket pricing.
"It's not a surcharge. It's going to be a fare increase. It's going to be more or less two percent higher than today's fare," she said.
